cf.title: skip check constraints verification for unaffected columns during UPDATE

input.subject: UPDATE run check constraints for affected columns only

verdict_reasoning: The decisive objection is demand-1: the proposal is a performance optimization, and the thread shows no benchmark, workload or user report. The patch adds a new rule on which CHECK enforcement depends, so a committer would likely ask for numbers before reading the design. Confidence is low because the verdict rests on absent evidence and only 3 of 12 messages are visible. The level 2 objections security-1 and maintenance-fit-1 survived but are not evaluated here.

brief.title: Skip check constraint verification for unaffected columns during update
brief.problem: Every UPDATE re-checks all CHECK constraints on the table, even ones that reference only columns the statement does not change. The author points to a Todo wiki item and an older thread. The thread does not quantify the cost or name the workloads that suffer from it.
brief.proposed_design: During UPDATE, the executor skips a CHECK constraint when none of its referenced columns is updated, including columns changed through stored generated columns. It never skips when a BEFORE ROW UPDATE trigger exists, or when the constraint is NOT VALID, NOT ENFORCED, has a whole-row reference, or references no columns. v7 keeps separate cached check expressions for INSERT and UPDATE, following the generated-column pattern, so MERGE with both actions stays correct.
user_visible_surface: New DEBUG1 log message: "skipping verification for constraint "%s" on table "%s"".
Changed C API in executor.h and execnodes.h: ResultRelInfo check-expression caching, likely split into INSERT and UPDATE arrays as in v7.
author_claims: A row that passed a constraint still passes it if no referenced column changes, so re-checking is unnecessary.
Skipping is safe when generated columns can be skipped, since the same BEFORE ROW UPDATE trigger guard applies.
Cross-partition UPDATE runs as DELETE plus INSERT, so it always checks all constraints.
Reviewer Florin Irion calls the core optimization sound, including trigger, generated-column and whole-row handling.
Reviewer solai v tested v8 and found no issues with UPDATE, MERGE, generated columns or triggers.
brief.thread_state: Tom Lane and li carol raised the trigger case, which v2 handles. Florin Irion and solai v reviewed later versions positively; v8 is in Needs review and has moved through five CommitFests with no committer reply.
unclear: No benchmark shows how much time the skip saves, or for which constraint shapes.
The thread does not say whether v8 keeps the v7 split arrays or the v6 rule that turns the skip off for all MERGE.
The thread does not say how INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE is covered in v8.
Nobody answers li carol's point that ExecSimpleRelationUpdate passes CMD_INSERT, or says whether logical replication apply gets the skip.
The thread does not say whether volatile or user-defined functions in a CHECK expression affect the skip.

objections.title: No measurement shows the skip saves meaningful time
objections.failure_scenario: A committer pushes the patch, and from then on every user relies on new skip logic to keep CHECK constraints enforced on UPDATE. Most CHECK expressions are cheap comparisons, so typical users may see no measurable gain. A future bug in the skip rules would let invalid rows into tables, and nobody would notice until queries or applications hit bad data.
objections.argument: The only demand shown is a Todo wiki item and an older thread (message #1). No user report, workload or benchmark appears in twelve messages, and the reviews in messages #9 and #12 check correctness, not speed. The change adds a correctness-critical path for constraint enforcement, with MERGE, ON CONFLICT and replication cases, so a committer would likely ask what users gain for that risk.
objections.author_must_show: Which constraint shapes and UPDATE workloads get a measurable speedup, and how large is it compared with the cost of the UPDATE itself?

critic.reasoning: The Todo item and the older thread show some lasting interest, but the thread has no benchmark, workload or user report. This fits a "show demand" outcome, which a measurement could answer.

other_surviving.title: Skipped checks that depend on session state change who can update a row
other_surviving.failure_scenario: An application uses `check (owner = current_user)` or a check that calls a stable or user-defined function to stop other roles from changing a row. After upgrading, role B runs `update t set note = 'x'`. The check references only `owner`, which is unchanged, so it is skipped and B's update succeeds where it failed before.
other_surviving.argument: The skip rule rests on the claim that a row which passed a constraint still passes it if no referenced column changes (commit message). That holds only when the expression depends on the row alone. Postgres documents that CHECK conditions should be immutable, but it does not enforce this, so expressions using `current_user`, settings or table lookups exist in the field. The exclusion list in v8 covers NOT VALID, NOT ENFORCED, whole-row and column-free constraints, but not non-immutable expressions, and the brief lists volatile and user-defined functions as unanswered.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Will v8 skip only constraints whose expressions are immutable, and if not, how will release notes warn users who rely on session-dependent checks?

critic.reasoning: Postgres accepts stable expressions such as current_user in a CHECK, and the v8 exclusion list does not cover them. The documented immutability assumption weakens the objection, but the generated-column precedent does not answer it, because generated columns enforce immutability.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: Skip rule depends on every caller passing the right command type
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a new path that changes a row through ExecConstraints with CMD_UPDATE, but some column changes are not in the updated-column set. The cached UPDATE check expressions then skip a constraint those changes affect. A row that violates the CHECK is stored, and nothing fails until a user finds bad data.
other_surviving.argument: After the patch, the correctness of CHECK enforcement depends on cmdtype and on ExecGetAllUpdatedCols being complete for every caller. The thread already shows this coupling is easy to miss: the shared ri_CheckConstraintExprs cache broke MERGE with both actions, and v6 and v7 fixed it in different ways (messages #8, #9, #10). Message #3 notes that ExecSimpleRelationUpdate passes CMD_INSERT, and no reply says whether logical replication apply is meant to get the skip. The thread does not name an assertion or test that fails when a new caller gets this wrong.
other_surviving.author_must_show: What makes a future caller that passes CMD_UPDATE with an incomplete updated-column set fail loudly, and is replication apply meant to be covered or excluded?

critic.reasoning: The guard copies ExecInitGenerated, which lowers the concern. But the shared cache broke MERGE during this thread, and no reply says whether apply is covered or what fails when a caller gets it wrong.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

refuted.title: Visible behavior change for CHECK constraints that call non-immutable functions
refuted.failure_scenario: A site has CHECK (valid_code(code)), where valid_code() reads a lookup table, and later tightens that function. Today, any UPDATE of such a row, even of an unrelated column, fails and exposes the bad row. After upgrade the same UPDATE succeeds, and the stale row stays hidden until someone updates code itself.
refuted.argument: The patch lets an UPDATE skip a CHECK constraint whose referenced columns are unchanged. It touches no documentation files and has no release-note text, so nothing tells users this behavior changed. Postgres already documents that CHECK expressions are assumed immutable, which weakens this objection. But such constraints exist in the field, and the brief notes that the thread never discusses volatile or user-defined functions in CHECK expressions.
refuted.author_must_show: Will v8 document the skip next to the existing immutability caveat for CHECK constraints, or keep checking constraints that call non-immutable functions?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of security-1. Both say the v8 exclusion list does not cover non-immutable CHECK expressions, and security-1 gives the more concrete case.

refuted.title: Logical apply path and the updated-column set behind the skip
refuted.failure_scenario: A subscriber has a CHECK constraint that the publisher lacks. The apply worker, or an extension that applies changes through ExecConstraints with CMD_UPDATE, builds an updated-column set that misses a column the incoming row changes. The check is skipped, and the subscriber stores a row that violates its own constraint without any error.
refuted.argument: v8 touches execReplication.c, but the thread does not say whether ExecSimpleRelationUpdate now passes CMD_UPDATE, which li carol asked about in message #3. The skip is safe only if ExecGetAllUpdatedCols is accurate on every path that calls ExecConstraints. On the apply path, that set is built from the replicated tuple rather than from parsed SET clauses, and the thread does not say how it is built. Extensions that build their own ResultRelInfo and RTE for apply face the same dependency.
refuted.author_must_show: Does logical replication apply get the skip in v8, and how is its updated-column set built so it always covers every column the applied row changes?

critic.reasoning: If ExecSimpleRelationUpdate still passes CMD_INSERT, apply skips nothing. If it passes CMD_UPDATE, the apply worker marks every replicated column except unchanged TOAST values as updated, so the set covers each changed column. maintenance-fit-1 keeps the open question.

refuted.title: No measurement shows the saving is worth a new executor invariant
refuted.failure_scenario: A committer takes on a second cached check-expression array per ResultRelInfo and a new skip rule in ExecRelCheck. Typical CHECK expressions cost little next to the heap update, index updates and WAL, so users see no measurable change. The project keeps the extra code path and its corner cases with no shown gain.
refuted.argument: Message #1 cites only a Todo item and an old thread, and the brief notes there is no benchmark and no named workload. Reviews in messages #9 and #12 test correctness, not speed. Without numbers for some constraint shape, such as many or costly CHECKs on wide tables, a committer would likely ask whether the gain justifies the liability. Five CommitFests with no committer reply also leave no clear owner for later fixes.
refuted.author_must_show: Which table and constraint shapes gain a measurable UPDATE speedup from the skip, and by how much on a standard benchmark?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of demand-1. Its extra point about no committer owner belongs to committability and must not support a desirability objection.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: The patch touches execReplication.c, and the thread does not say whether logical replication apply gets the skip.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch changes the ResultRelInfo check-expression cache in execnodes.h and declarations in executor.h.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: A skipped CHECK such as `check (owner = current_user)` changes which role can update a row.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: CHECK enforcement on UPDATE now depends on the command type and a complete updated-column set in every caller.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The skip decision sits in the constraint check that every UPDATE on a table with CHECK constraints runs.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which constraint shapes and UPDATE workloads get a measurable speedup from the skip, and how large is it compared with the cost of the UPDATE itself?
Does v8 skip a CHECK whose expression is not immutable, such as `check (owner = current_user)`, and if so, how are users told?
Does logical replication apply get the skip in v8, and does ExecSimpleRelationUpdate still pass CMD_INSERT to ExecConstraints?
What fails loudly when a future caller passes CMD_UPDATE with an incomplete updated-column set?
Does v8 keep the separate INSERT and UPDATE cached arrays from v7, and how does it cover INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows the executor's ModifyTable and constraint code would have to own it. Tom Lane asked one question in message #2, and the brief reports no committer reply to later versions.
committability.liability: The owner signs for CHECK enforcement on every UPDATE, MERGE, ON CONFLICT and apply path, with no time limit. A bug in the skip rule stores invalid rows without an error.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted eight versions, answered reviewers, and moved the entry through five CommitFests, which suggests the author stays for fixes.

not_now.evidence_that_would_change_it: A benchmark that shows a measurable UPDATE speedup for a named constraint shape, such as many or costly CHECK constraints on a wide table, compared with total UPDATE cost. A user report of CHECK re-evaluation as a bottleneck would also help.

priority.reason: The idea follows the existing generated-column skip pattern and no surviving objection is fatal, but the thread shows no number for the gain. The patch is small (about 15 KB) but touches constraint enforcement in the executor, so review should wait for a benchmark.

provisional_note: Without the code, this review cannot confirm how v8 builds the updated-column set on each path, or whether it treats non-immutable CHECK expressions specially. Messages #4 to #12 were not visible, so some of the questions may already have answers there.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

Revert structural changes to not-null constraints

precedents_retrieved.objection:
There are some problems with the new way to handle these constraints
that were detected at the last minute, and require fixes that appear too
invasive to be doing this late in the cycle.  Revert this (again) for
now, we'll try again with these problems fixed.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add support for ON UPDATE/DELETE actions on ALTER CONSTRAINT
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch extends alter table ... alter constraint so it can change the ON UPDATE and ON DELETE actions of a foreign key. It also changes alter constraint to keep the deferrability options the user did not name, and later added an alter constraint ... set variant that changes only the named properties.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the same deferrability syntax should not mean different things depending on the constraint's previous state, and suggested full replacement or a new add or replace constraint command. Wolfgang Walther objected that the SET variant had the same implied-change problem and proposed separate per-action foreign key syntax. The thread reached no agreement on the syntax, and David Steele returned the patch because it had not been updated for over a year and no longer applied.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The main issue I've got though is a definitional one --- I'm not at all sold on your premise that constraint deferrability syntax should mean different things depending on the previous state of the constraint.

precedents_retrieved.title: CHECK constraint deferrable Support
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets CHECK constraints be declared DEFERRABLE and INITIALLY DEFERRED, as the SQL standard allows, so SET CONSTRAINTS can delay a CHECK until commit. Rows that fail a deferrable CHECK are rechecked at commit time.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the CHECK implementation assumes constraints are immutable, and the patch does not change that assumption, so he called the feature a toy. Others then argued it should be dropped or combined with deferrable NOT NULL, which Robert Haas and Vik Fearing disputed. Dean Rasheed also reported open bugs, including a deferred constraint that still failed immediately and a wrong constraint-exclusion result. The visible messages do not show why the author withdrew the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I continue to assert that basing this feature on the current CHECK implementation will produce nothing but a toy feature, that's not only of little practical use but will be an active foot-gun for people who expect it to do more than it can.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix permission tests for views/tables proven empty by constraint exclusion.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Fix permission tests for views/tables proven empty by constraint exclusion.
Reverted commit(s): Add regression test for bug fixed by recent refactoring.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
A view defined as "select <something> where false" had the curious property
that the system wouldn't check whether users had the privileges necessary
to select from it.  More generally, permissions checks could be skipped
for tables referenced in sub-selects or views that were proven empty by
constraint exclusion (although some quick testing suggests this seldom
happens in cases of practical interest).  This happened because the planner
failed to include rangetable entries for such tables in the finished plan.

This was noticed in connection with erroneous handling of materialized
views, but actually the issue is quite unrelated to matviews.  Therefore,
revert commit 200ba1667b3a8d7a9d559d2f05f83d209c9d8267 in favor of a more
direct test for the real problem.

Back-patch to 9.2 where the bug was introduced (by commit
7741dd6590073719688891898e85f0cb73453159).

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow AddForeignUpdateTargets to add extra target expressions other than columns
precedents_retrieved.summary: postgres_fdw identifies remote rows for non-direct UPDATE and DELETE by ctid alone, so when the remote table is partitioned or has inheritance children, rows in other children with the same ctid are also changed. The patch lets AddForeignUpdateTargets add extra target expressions that are not columns, implemented as Params that carry the remote tableoid up to ModifyTable, so the remote statement can also filter on tableoid.
precedents_retrieved.objection: An earlier approach that expanded the tuple descriptor with junk columns was dropped. Etsuro Fujita said it broke the planner assumption that rel->max_attr matches the catalog and could slow down foreign scans. The Param-based patch then drew a review comment from Tom Lane, shown only as a quote, suggesting that FDWs be allowed to define extra system column IDs instead. Fujita agreed with that comment but found no clear way to implement it, did not have time in the v13 cycle, and marked the entry Returned with feedback after it had waited on author for several commitfests.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I 100% agree with Tom, and actually, I tried to address his comments, but I haven't come up with a clear solution for that yet.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve amcheck to check UNIQUE constraint in btree index
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Peter Geoghegan, Mark Dilger, David Steele
precedents_retrieved.summary: Extend contrib/amcheck's bt_index_check and bt_index_parent_check so that, for btree indexes with a UNIQUE constraint, they detect duplicate keys whose heap tuples are visible, including duplicates spanning adjacent leaf pages, and report the index and heap TIDs involved. Later versions added an optional argument to enable the uniqueness check and a regression test variant for 32-bit systems.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers asked for further changes: Peter Geoghegan objected to reporting violations as WARNINGs, to the message saying an index only might be corrupt (calling it an unacceptable false positive), to the handling of cross-page duplicates, and to tests that update pg_index, and suggested opclass-based fault injection and sharing the heapallindexed snapshot. Mark Dilger's review of v4 asked for documentation updates, pg_amcheck integration with TAP tests, and a different test approach. No updated patch followed for several weeks, and David Steele marked it Returned with Feedback because it needed more work and had not been updated.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This patch appears to need some work and has not been updated in several
weeks, so marking Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Change a constraint's index - ALTER TABLE ... ALTER CONSTRAINT ... USING INDEX ...
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Alvaro Herrera, Laurenz Albe
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds ALTER TABLE ... ALTER CONSTRAINT ... USING INDEX to replace the index behind an EXCLUDE, UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY or FOREIGN KEY constraint with a similar index. The main use case is swapping a primary key index for one with INCLUDE columns, or back.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane wanted the feature rejected because a primary key with a swapped index is no longer an accurate primary key, and information_schema cannot describe it. Alvaro Herrera and Laurenz Albe agreed that primary keys with INCLUDE columns would first need PRIMARY KEY syntax, so that pg_dump works. That leaves this command a narrow use case. The author did not answer the review, and Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
TBH I think if we really wanted the feature of primary keys with
included columns, we'd have to add it to the PRIMARY KEY syntax rather
than having an ad-hoc ALTER TABLE ALTER CONSTRAINT USING INDEX command
to replace the index underneath.

precedents_retrieved.title: Optimizing NULL check on pkey column
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes the planner fold IS NULL and IS NOT NULL checks on primary key columns, and later also on NOT NULL constraint columns, into constants at planning time. It does this only when the column is not on the nullable side of an outer join.
precedents_retrieved.objection: David Rowley said the patch looks up attnotnull by opening the table in eval_const_expressions, which is not acceptable, and pointed to Andy Fan's patch that caches this in RelOptInfo. He said new NULL-tracking logic should wait for better planner infrastructure being built for UniqueKeys and related work, and proposed to return the patch with feedback. The author did not reply, so Jaime Casanova closed the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I agree that we should delay adding any
new smarts in regards to NULL or NOT NULL until we have some more
robust infrastructure to make this sort of patch easier and cheaper.

precedents_retrieved.title: avoid bitmapOR-ing indexes for scan conditions implied by partition constraint
precedents_retrieved.authors: Justin Pryzby (justinpryzby), Soumyadeep Chakraborty (soumyadeep2007), Soumyadeep Chakraborty (soumyadeepc)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes the planner skip bitmap index scans for arms of an OR clause that the partition constraint refutes, so each partition scans only the useful arms. The change lives in generate_bitmap_or_paths() in indxpath.c and targets queries with long OR lists over many partitions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected to fixing this in indxpath.c. The fix helps only bitmap scans, may repeat the same proof, cannot be turned off, leaves row estimates unchanged, and may break the loop that requires each OR arm to match an index. He proposed removing proven quals from baserestrictinfo instead, but measured about 2.5% slowdown on pgbench -S and left the direction open. The entry then sat in Waiting on Author for weeks, and Masahiko Sawada returned it with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I really quite dislike solving
this via a kluge in indxpath.c.

precedents_retrieved.title: Lock updated tuples in tuple_update() and tuple_delete()
precedents_retrieved.summary: When tuple_update() or tuple_delete() finds a concurrently updated tuple in read committed mode, the table AM locks the updated version itself instead of returning TM_Updated for a separate tuple_lock() call. Later versions also had update and delete return the old tuple through a slot passed by the executor, which avoids refetching it and helps table AMs with costly TID lookups.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Version 15 was committed in March 2023, then reverted after Andres Freund's post-commit review. He showed that RETURNING could use the wrong tuple, with an isolation test that fails. He also criticised the new API: the ignored wait parameter, tmfd turned into an input, and the LazyTupleTableSlot code. The redesigned old-tuple API came days before the version 16 feature freeze, and he said it was not ready for 16. In March 2024 the author planned to push a revised version, and the visible messages do not show why the entry was finally returned with feedback in October 2024.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I guess this really is part of my issue with this change - it optimizes the rare case, while not addressing the same inefficiency in the common case.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix index-only scan plans, take 2.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Fix index-only scan plans, take 2.
Reverted commit(s): Fix index-only scan plans when not all index columns can be returned.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 4ace45677 failed to fix the problem fully, because the
same issue of attempting to fetch a non-returnable index column
can occur when rechecking the indexqual after using a lossy index
operator.  Moreover, it broke EXPLAIN for such indexquals (which
indicates a gap in our test cases :-().

Revert the code changes of 4ace45677 in favor of adding a new field
to struct IndexOnlyScan, containing a version of the indexqual that
can be executed against the index-returned tuple without using any
non-returnable columns.  (The restrictions imposed by check_index_only
guarantee this is possible, although we may have to recompute indexed
expressions.)  Support construction of that during setrefs.c
processing by marking IndexOnlyScan.indextlist entries as resjunk
if they can't be returned, rather than removing them entirely.
(We could alternatively require setrefs.c to look up the IndexOptInfo
again, but abusing resjunk this way seems like a reasonably safe way
to avoid needing to do that.)

This solution isn't great from an API-stability standpoint: if there
are any extensions out there that build IndexOnlyScan structs directly,
they'll be broken in the next minor releases.  However, only a very
invasive extension would be likely to do such a thing.  There's no
change in the Path representation, so typical planner extensions
shouldn't have a problem.

As before, back-patch to all supported branches.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix pg_get_constraintdef for NOT NULL constraints on domains
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Fix pg_get_constraintdef for NOT NULL constraints on domains
Reverted commit(s): Revert structural changes to not-null constraints
precedents_retrieved.objection:
We added pg_constraint rows for all not-null constraints, first for
tables and later for domains; but while the ones for tables were
reverted, the ones for domains were not.  However, we did accidentally
revert ruleutils.c support for the ones on domains in 6f8bb7c1e961,

This is only needed in branch 17, because we've reinstated this code in
branch master with commit 14e87ffa5c54.  Add some new tests in both
branches.

I couldn't find anything else that needs de-reverting.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Avoid the creation of the free space map for small heap relations".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Avoid the creation of the free space map for small heap relations".
Reverted commit(s): Improve code comments in b0eaa4c51b.; Avoid creation of the free space map for small heap relations, take 2.; During pg_upgrade, conditionally skip transfer of FSMs.; Add more tests for FSM.; Clear the local map when not used.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This feature was using a process local map to track the first few blocks
in the relation.  The map was reset each time we get the block with enough
freespace.  It was discussed that it would be better to track this map on
a per-relation basis in relcache and then invalidate the same whenever
vacuum frees up some space in the page or when FSM is created.  The new
design would be better both in terms of API design and performance.

List of commits reverted, in reverse chronological order:

06c8a5090e  Improve code comments in b0eaa4c51b.
13e8643bfc  During pg_upgrade, conditionally skip transfer of FSMs.
6f918159a9  Add more tests for FSM.
9c32e4c350  Clear the local map when not used.
29d108cdec  Update the documentation for FSM behavior..

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found in the list. Message #1 links an older thread and a Todo wiki item but does not say what that thread concluded or why the idea stalled, so no earlier rejection reason can be checked against this proposal.

Apart from the behavior change above, the patch adds no syntax, GUC, catalog state or dumped object. Its only new user-visible output is a DEBUG1 message, so it raises no pg_dump, psql or SQL-standard issue.

The proposal changes no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog or wire protocol, so pg_upgrade and physical standbys are unaffected. The ResultRelInfo change in execnodes.h is a normal major-version API change, and nobody has proposed backpatching it.

Apart from the non-immutable expression case, the change adds no new privilege, role or exposed data. The DEBUG1 message reveals only constraint and table names to someone who can already update the table.
Fit in core is reasonable, since the change follows the existing generated-column skip pattern; objections cover maintainability and unshown benefit.

Postgres has no feature, setting or documented idiom that skips CHECK evaluation for unchanged columns, and an extension cannot change ExecConstraints without forking executor code. The patch reuses the existing generated-column skip rule (ExecGetAllUpdatedCols, the BEFORE ROW UPDATE trigger guard, the I/U cached arrays) and does not add a second mechanism.
Only one objection. The Todo item is weak but real evidence of interest, and the benefit would reach all users with CHECK constraints, so a precise answer here is "not now, show measurements".
